rest-post.kotlin-okhttp:
import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody

fun main() {
    val client = OkHttpClient()
    val body = "{\"id\":7,\"item\":\"it's \\\"quoted\\\" \$x\"}".toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
    val request = Request.Builder()
        .url("https://api.example.com/orders/7")
        .method("PUT", body)
        .addHeader("X-Trace", "abc")
        .build()
    client.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
        println("${response.code} ${response.body?.string()}")
    }
}

grpc-unary.python-grpc:
# Uses the modules grpc_tools.protoc generates from your .proto; they are named after the .proto file, shown here as greeter_pb2 / greeter_pb2_grpc.

import grpc
from google.protobuf import json_format

import greeter_pb2
import greeter_pb2_grpc

channel = grpc.insecure_channel("localhost:5001")
stub = greeter_pb2_grpc.GreeterStub(channel)
request = json_format.Parse("{\"name\":\"world\"}", greeter_pb2.HelloRequest())
metadata = [("x-api-key", "k")]

response = stub.SayHello(request, metadata=metadata, timeout=30)
print(json_format.MessageToJson(response))

grpc-server-stream.python-grpc:
# Uses the modules grpc_tools.protoc generates from your .proto; they are named after the .proto file, shown here as greeter_pb2 / greeter_pb2_grpc.

import grpc
from google.protobuf import json_format

import greeter_pb2
import greeter_pb2_grpc

channel = grpc.secure_channel("grpc.example.com:443", grpc.ssl_channel_credentials())
stub = greeter_pb2_grpc.GreeterStub(channel)
request = json_format.Parse("{\"name\":\"world\",\"count\":3}", greeter_pb2.HelloRequest())
metadata = []

for response in stub.SayHellos(request, metadata=metadata):
    print(json_format.MessageToJson(response))

websocket.python-websockets:
import asyncio

import websockets


async def main():
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:5000/ws/echo", additional_headers={}) as ws:
        await ws.send("{\"type\":\"ping\"}")
        async for message in ws:
            print(message)


asyncio.run(main())

mqtt-publish.python-paho:
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

client = mqtt.Client(mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)
client.connect("broker.example.com", 1883)
client.loop_start()
info = client.publish("sensors/temp", "21.5", qos=1, retain=True)
info.wait_for_publish()
client.loop_stop()
client.disconnect()

mqtt-subscribe.python-paho:
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt


def on_message(client, userdata, message):
    print(message.topic, message.payload.decode())


client = mqtt.Client(mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)
client.on_message = on_message
client.connect("broker.example.com", 1883)
client.subscribe("sensors/#", qos=0)
client.loop_forever()

nats-request.python-nats:
import asyncio

import nats


async def main():
    nc = await nats.connect("nats://localhost:4222")
    msg = await nc.request("orders.get", "{\"id\":7}".encode(), timeout=5)
    print(msg.data.decode())
    await nc.drain()


asyncio.run(main())

nats-jetstream.python-nats:
import asyncio

import nats


async def main():
    nc = await nats.connect("nats://localhost:4222")
    js = nc.jetstream()
    ack = await js.publish("orders.created", "new".encode())
    print(ack.stream, ack.seq)
    await nc.drain()


asyncio.run(main())

socketio-emit.python-socketio:
import json

import socketio

sio = socketio.Client()


@sio.event
def connect():
    sio.emit("chat", json.loads("{\"text\":\"hi\"}"))


sio.connect("http://localhost:3000", headers={})
sio.wait()
